K1.stone_why: Faceted bowls and flat-cut curves in a classical serif read clearly as a cut inscription without losing the serif's dignity.
K1.carving_why: Facets are applied evenly across lower case, capitals and digits so it reads as one design, and 1/7, 3/8, 0/O stay distinct, though at the largest size some facets look more polygon-sampled than chiselled.
K1.calm_why: Steady and measured with good presence; the faceting adds a slight restlessness to the bold numerals.
K1.personality_why: A recognisable hewn-serif voice, but close to its siblings and to its smooth source.

K2.stone_why: Only a light hint of faceting on curves, so it reads mostly as a polished book serif with a faint chiselled edge.
K2.carving_why: Coherent and clean but so subtle at display size that the cuts read as slight low-resolution flattening rather than deliberate chisel strokes.
K2.calm_why: Very calm and composed while the bold weights still carry presence.
K2.personality_why: A small step away from a generic serif; easy to mistake for the uncarved face.

K3.stone_why: Smooth classical serif; any inscriptional feeling comes from the Roman proportions alone, not from carving.
K3.carving_why: No visible carving; curves are fully smooth.
K3.calm_why: Calm, even and authoritative with ample presence in the bold numbers.
K3.personality_why: Handsome but anonymous text serif; nothing you would recognise again as its own.

K4.stone_why: Same clear faceted-curve treatment as K1, giving a convincing cut-stone reading at title sizes.
K4.carving_why: Consistent facets across all glyphs with crisp corners and unambiguous digits, though the large bowls still look slightly polygonal rather than V-cut.
K4.calm_why: Steady with presence; facets add mild visual energy without aggression.
K4.personality_why: Distinct hewn character, practically indistinguishable from K1.

K5.stone_why: Stronger, irregular facets make it feel rough-hewn from rock, especially in the bold S and numerals.
K5.carving_why: Facets vary in size from glyph to glyph (lumpy S, uneven 0 and 5), which edges toward broken or processed rather than one controlled chisel; digits remain legible.
K5.calm_why: Still grounded and not shouting, but the irregular outlines make the bold numbers a bit restless.
K5.personality_why: More rugged and memorable than K1/K4, though part of the character comes from apparent randomness.

K6.stone_why: Heavy, wide, slab-like weight plus rough facets reads most strongly as hewn stone blocks.
K6.carving_why: Facet treatment is coherent in spirit but uneven in execution (bumpy S, 5 and 0 outlines), and the heavy weight fills counters; digits still distinguishable.
K6.calm_why: Heavy everywhere, including the regular titles and the body text, so it feels loud and dense rather than calm.
K6.personality_why: Unmistakable: a dark, rugged monumental voice clearly different from the other six.

K7.stone_why: Strong rough faceting gives a rough-hewn rock feel, like K5.
K7.carving_why: Irregular facet sizes on S, 0 and 5 read partly as processing artefacts rather than deliberate cuts, though the design is applied to every glyph and digits stay clear.
K7.calm_why: Grounded with presence, slightly restless in the bold set numbers.
K7.personality_why: Rugged and recognisable, essentially the same voice as K5.
